direct_dependents: every .claude/transfers/*.json the Stop hook inspects, in every repository
the source_cleanup branch three lines below, which already models this for the source
layer.release_boundary: hook file; effective on the next Stop event, no deploy and no service
state_or_contract: a verified transfer's destination must exist, unless a destination cleanup is recorded planned and performed, in which case it must be gone

notes: The guard was not merely inconvenient - it made leaving a stale scratch directory the cheapest compliant option, which is the shape of a rule people learn to route around.

observed.actual: the Stop guard refused with 'destination is absent' on a contract I had just cleaned up correctly, having refused two passes earlier because the copy was still being written to. Two refusals on one contract, pointing opposite ways.
observed.expected: a transfer whose product was scratch can be closed once the scratch is cleaned up

plan.causal_hypothesis: the destination check had no cleanup concept while the source check three lines below it did, so the guard modelled every transfer as leaving a permanent product. A transfer whose product is scratch fell outside its world: it could be honest or it could be closed, not both.
fix_steps: give the destination the inversion the source already has
add the paired tests this file's own convention calls for, one per direction
prove them red against the reverted rule before accepting their green

summary: A verified transfer whose destination was deliberately disposed of could not be closed: the guard required the destination to exist, so the only options were a false record or scratch left on disk forever.
